comparisons.peer_topic: Non-U.S. Pension Plan Assets and Obligations
comparisons.peer_summary: As of November 3, 2024, non-U.S. pension plan assets totaled $229 million, with projected and accumulated benefit obligations of $260 million and $229 million, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose specific metrics for non-U.S. pension plan assets and obligations, highlighting that non-U.S. plans hold significant value. Intel reports $1.7 billion in accumulated benefit obligations for non-US plans and 60% of total plan assets located outside the US, with these non-US plans having obligations exceeding assets. Similarly, Broadcom reports $229 million in assets for non-U.S. pension plans, with projected benefit obligations of $260 million and accumulated benefit obligations of $229 million for those same plans. Both disclosures focus on the financial health and geographic distribution of international pension liabilities.

sentences.text: As of December 28, 2024, the accumulated benefit obligations were $763 million and $1.7 billion for the US plan and non-US plans, respectively.
[footnote 2] The fair value of plan assets was approximately 40% in the US and 60% outside of the US as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, only non-US plans had projected benefit obligations and accumulated benefit obligations in excess of plan assets.
The fair value of pension plan assets as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $229 million and $204 million, respectively, of assets for our non-U.S. pension plans.
The projected benefit obligations as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $260 million and $202 million, respectively, of obligations related to our non-U.S. pension plans.
The accumulated benefit obligations as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $229 million and $188 million, respectively, of obligations related to our non-U.S. pension plans.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the projected benefit obligations of the company's pension plans were $191 million with plan assets of $261 million, compared to $175 million in obligations and $232 million in assets as of August 31, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and Intel both disclose projected benefit obligations and plan assets for their pension plans, noting that their plans are located at various foreign sites. Intel reports $763 million in US accumulated benefit obligations and $1.7 billion for non-US plans as of Dec 28, 2024. Micron reports total projected benefit obligations of $191 million and plan assets of $261 million as of Aug 29, 2024, specifically for its foreign sites. Both companies provide specific monetary values for these pension obligations and assets, allowing for a comparison of the scale of their international pension liabilities.
